mustKnow.en: Heap (unordered) file: insert is O(1) at end, but search is O(n) full scan.
mustKnow.bn: Heap (unordered) file: insert শেষে O(1), কিন্তু search O(n) full scan।

mustKnow.en: Sequential file: records sorted by key; binary search O(log n), but insert needs shifting/overflow.
mustKnow.bn: Sequential file: record key অনুযায়ী sorted; binary search O(log n), কিন্তু insert-এ shifting/overflow লাগে।

mustKnow.en: Hashed file: h(k)=k mod N gives O(1) equality search, but no range query support.
mustKnow.bn: Hashed file: h(k)=k mod N দিয়ে equality search O(1), কিন্তু range query হয় না।

mustKnow.en: Storage ladder: Bit → Byte → Block/Page → File → Database; disk I/O is counted in blocks, not records.
mustKnow.bn: Storage ladder: Bit → Byte → Block/Page → File → Database; disk I/O block-এ গোনা হয়, record-এ নয়।

mustKnow.en: Dense index = one entry per record; sparse index = one entry per block (only on an ordered file).
mustKnow.bn: Dense index = প্রতি record-এ একটি entry; sparse index = প্রতি block-এ একটি entry (শুধু ordered file-এ)।

mustKnow.en: Primary index is on the ordering key and can be sparse; secondary index is on a non-ordering field and must be dense.
mustKnow.bn: Primary index ordering key-এর উপর, sparse হতে পারে; secondary index non-ordering field-এর উপর, dense হতেই হয়।

mustKnow.en: A table has at most ONE clustered index (it fixes physical row order) but many non-clustered ones.
mustKnow.bn: একটি table-এ সর্বোচ্চ একটি clustered index (physical row order ঠিক করে) কিন্তু অনেক non-clustered থাকতে পারে।

mustKnow.en: B+ tree: all keys (with record pointers) live in the leaves; internal nodes only route the search.
mustKnow.bn: B+ tree: সব key (record pointer সহ) leaf-এ থাকে; internal node শুধু search route করে।

mustKnow.en: B+ tree order n: a node holds up to n pointers and n-1 keys; it is balanced, all leaves at the same level.
mustKnow.bn: B+ tree order n: একটি node-এ সর্বোচ্চ n pointer ও n-1 key; এটি balanced, সব leaf একই level-এ।

mustKnow.en: B+ tree leaves are chained in sorted order, so range queries (BETWEEN) just scan the leaf chain.
mustKnow.bn: B+ tree-এর leaf গুলো sorted ক্রমে linked, তাই range query (BETWEEN) শুধু leaf chain scan করে।

mustKnow.en: B-tree stores data pointers in every node; B+ tree keeps them only in leaves, giving higher fan-out and a shorter tree.
mustKnow.bn: B-tree প্রতি node-এ data pointer রাখে; B+ tree শুধু leaf-এ রাখে, ফলে fan-out বেশি ও tree ছোট।

mustKnow.en: Extendible hashing: directory of 2^(global depth) entries; a bucket splits locally, directory doubles only when local depth = global depth.
mustKnow.bn: Extendible hashing: 2^(global depth) entry-র directory; bucket local-ভাবে split হয়, directory শুধু তখন double হয় যখন local depth = global depth।

mustKnow.en: Static hashing suffers overflow/underflow as data grows; dynamic hashing (extendible, linear) grows the bucket space on demand.
mustKnow.bn: Static hashing-এ data বাড়লে overflow/underflow হয়; dynamic hashing (extendible, linear) প্রয়োজনে bucket space বাড়ায়।

mustKnow.en: Query processing order: Parser → translation to relational algebra → Optimizer (chooses a plan) → Execution engine → Result.
mustKnow.bn: Query processing ক্রম: Parser → relational algebra-তে অনুবাদ → Optimizer (plan বাছে) → Execution engine → Result।

mustKnow.en: Cost of a plan is dominated by disk-block I/O; optimizers compare plans by estimated block reads using table statistics.
mustKnow.bn: একটি plan-এর cost মূলত disk-block I/O দিয়ে নির্ধারিত; optimizer table statistics দিয়ে আনুমানিক block read তুলনা করে।

mustKnow.en: Heuristic (rule-based) optimization pushes SELECT and PROJECT down the query tree to shrink rows/columns early.
mustKnow.bn: Heuristic (rule-based) optimization query tree-তে SELECT ও PROJECT নিচে ঠেলে আগেই row/column কমায়।

mustKnow.en: Bitmap indexes suit LOW-cardinality columns (gender, yes/no); B+ tree suits high-cardinality and range columns.
mustKnow.bn: Bitmap index LOW-cardinality column-এ (gender, yes/no) ভালো; B+ tree high-cardinality ও range column-এ ভালো।

mustKnow.en: OLTP = many short read/write transactions (normalized); OLAP/warehouse = few large read-only analytical queries (denormalized).
mustKnow.bn: OLTP = অনেক ছোট read/write transaction (normalized); OLAP/warehouse = অল্প বড় read-only analytical query (denormalized)।

mustKnow.en: Star schema: one fact table + denormalized dimensions; snowflake schema normalizes the dimensions into sub-tables.
mustKnow.bn: Star schema: একটি fact table + denormalized dimension; snowflake schema dimension-কে sub-table-এ normalize করে।

mustKnow.en: ETL = Extract, Transform, Load — the pipeline that feeds cleaned source data into a data warehouse.
mustKnow.bn: ETL = Extract, Transform, Load — যে pipeline পরিষ্কার source data data warehouse-এ আনে।

mustKnow.en: Data mining tasks: classification (supervised), clustering (unsupervised), association rules (Apriori), regression.
mustKnow.bn: Data mining task: classification (supervised), clustering (unsupervised), association rule (Apriori), regression।

mustKnow.en: Apriori: support(X)=transactions containing X ÷ total; confidence(X→Y)=support(X∪Y) ÷ support(X); subset of a frequent set is frequent (downward closure).
mustKnow.bn: Apriori: support(X)=X-যুক্ত transaction ÷ total; confidence(X→Y)=support(X∪Y) ÷ support(X); frequent set-এর subset-ও frequent (downward closure)।

formulas.formula: bfr = floor(B / R);  blocks = ceil(records / bfr)

question.en: 30,000 records of 100 B each in 1024 B blocks (unspanned). How many data blocks?
question.bn: 1024 B block-এ 100 B-এর 30,000 record (unspanned)। কতটি data block?

working.bn: bfr = floor(1024/100) = প্রতি block-এ 10 record; block = ceil(30000/10) = 3000।

formulas.formula: index entries = data blocks;  index blocks = ceil(data_blocks / floor(B / entry_size))

question.en: 3000 data blocks; sparse index entry = 15 B (9 B key + 6 B pointer) in 1024 B blocks. Index blocks?
question.bn: 3000 data block; sparse index entry = 15 B (9 B key + 6 B pointer), 1024 B block-এ। Index block?

working.en: entries/block = floor(1024/15) = 68; index blocks = ceil(3000/68) = ceil(44.1) = 45.
working.bn: প্রতি block entry = floor(1024/15) = 68; index block = ceil(3000/68) = ceil(44.1) = 45।

example.answer: 45 index blocks (binary-searched in ceil(log2 45)+1 = 7 block reads)

formulas.formula: repeat blocks = ceil(blocks / fan-out) until blocks = 1; number of repeats = index levels

question.en: First-level sparse index = 45 blocks, fan-out 68. How many index levels, and the search cost?
question.bn: First-level sparse index = 45 block, fan-out 68। কতটি index level এবং search cost কত?

working.en: Level 2 = ceil(45/68) = 1 block (the top). So 2 index levels. Search = 1 (L2) + 1 (L1) + 1 (data) = 3 block reads.
working.bn: Level 2 = ceil(45/68) = 1 block (top)। তাই 2টি index level। Search = 1 (L2) + 1 (L1) + 1 (data) = 3 block read।

example.answer: 2 index levels; 3 block reads vs 7 for a single-level sparse index

title.en: B+ tree node order from block size
title.bn: Block size থেকে B+ tree node order

formulas.formula: internal node order n:  n·P + (n-1)·K ≤ B   (P = block pointer, K = key)

question.en: Block B = 512 B, key K = 9 B, block pointer P = 6 B. Maximum order n of an internal node?
question.bn: Block B = 512 B, key K = 9 B, block pointer P = 6 B। Internal node-এর সর্বোচ্চ order n?

example.answer: n = 34 (so up to 34 pointers and 33 keys per internal node)

title.en: B+ tree leaf capacity & max record pointers
title.bn: B+ tree leaf capacity ও max record pointer

formulas.formula: leaf: p_leaf·(K + Pr) + P_next ≤ B;  for order n, a leaf holds up to n-1 keys/record pointers

question.en: A B+ tree index has n = 100. What is the maximum number of record pointers in a leaf? (BUET M.Sc. 2021)
question.bn: একটি B+ tree index-এর n = 100। একটি leaf-এ সর্বোচ্চ কতটি record pointer? (BUET M.Sc. 2021)

working.en: A node of order n holds at most n pointers and n-1 keys. A leaf stores one record pointer per key plus one next-leaf pointer, so max record pointers = n - 1 = 99.
working.bn: order n-এর node-এ সর্বোচ্চ n pointer ও n-1 key। Leaf প্রতি key-তে একটি record pointer রাখে, সাথে একটি next-leaf pointer, তাই সর্বোচ্চ record pointer = n - 1 = 99।

title.en: B+ tree height / levels for N keys
title.bn: N key-র জন্য B+ tree height / level

formulas.formula: levels ≈ ceil(log_fanout(N));  disk accesses to reach a record = tree height

question.en: Order 100, 1,000,000 keys. How many levels (max disk accesses) to reach a record?
question.bn: Order 100, 1,000,000 key। একটি record-এ পৌঁছাতে কতটি level (সর্বোচ্চ disk access)?

formulas.formula: directory entries = 2^(global depth);  double the directory only when a full bucket has local depth = global depth

question.en: Start global depth 1 (2 buckets), bucket capacity 2, hash = low-order bits. Insert 2,3,5,8,4,7. Final global depth & bucket count?
question.bn: Global depth 1 (2 bucket), bucket capacity 2, hash = low-order bit দিয়ে শুরু। 2,3,5,8,4,7 insert করো। শেষ global depth ও bucket সংখ্যা?

working.en: Even keys {2,8,4} and odd keys {3,5,7} overflow their depth-1 buckets. Each full bucket has local depth = global depth, so the directory doubles to global depth 2; buckets split on bit 2 into 00:{8,4}, 10:{2}, 01:{5}, 11:{3,7}.
working.bn: Even key {2,8,4} ও odd key {3,5,7} depth-1 bucket overflow করে। প্রতিটি full bucket-এর local depth = global depth, তাই directory double হয়ে global depth 2; bit 2-তে split হয়ে 00:{8,4}, 10:{2}, 01:{5}, 11:{3,7}।

formulas.formula: min buckets = ceil(records / bucket_capacity);  with load factor L: ceil(records / (capacity·L))

question.en: 10,000 records, 20 records/bucket, target load factor 0.8. Minimum buckets?
question.bn: 10,000 record, প্রতি bucket 20 record, target load factor 0.8। সর্বনিম্ন bucket?

working.en: Tight packing = ceil(10000/20) = 500; at load factor 0.8 = ceil(10000/(20·0.8)) = ceil(625) = 625.
working.bn: Tight packing = ceil(10000/20) = 500; load factor 0.8-এ = ceil(10000/(20·0.8)) = ceil(625) = 625।

title.en: Join cost: block nested-loop vs sort-merge
title.bn: Join cost: block nested-loop বনাম sort-merge

formulas.formula: BNL (1-block buffer, smaller relation outer) = b_outer + b_outer · b_inner;  sort-merge (already sorted) = b_r + b_s

question.en: R = 400 blocks, S = 100 blocks, one-block buffer. Block nested-loop cost (best choice of outer) vs sort-merge if both are sorted on the join key?
question.bn: R = 400 block, S = 100 block, one-block buffer। Block nested-loop cost (outer-এর সেরা বাছাই) বনাম sort-merge যদি দুটোই join key-তে sorted?

working.en: Make the smaller relation S the outer: cost = b_S + b_S·b_R = 100 + 100·400 = 40,100 block I/Os. If both are already sorted, sort-merge just merges: b_R + b_S = 400 + 100 = 500.
working.bn: ছোট relation S-কে outer করো: cost = b_S + b_S·b_R = 100 + 100·400 = 40,100 block I/O। দুটোই আগে থেকে sorted হলে sort-merge শুধু merge করে: b_R + b_S = 400 + 100 = 500।

example.answer: BNL ≈ 40,100 block I/Os; sort-merge (pre-sorted) = 500 — far cheaper

formulas.formula: support(X) = count(X) / N;  confidence(X→Y) = support(X∪Y) / support(X)

question.en: 5 baskets: {M,O,N,K,E,Y},{D,O,N,K,E,Y},{M,A,K,E},{M,U,C,K,Y},{C,O,O,K,I,E}, minsup 60% (count 3), minconf 70%. Is O,K→E a strong rule?
question.bn: 5টি basket: {M,O,N,K,E,Y},{D,O,N,K,E,Y},{M,A,K,E},{M,U,C,K,Y},{C,O,O,K,I,E}, minsup 60% (count 3), minconf 70%। O,K→E কি strong rule?

working.en: count{O,K}=3, count{O,K,E}=3. support{O,K,E}=3/5=60% ≥ minsup. confidence = support{O,K,E}/support{O,K} = 3/3 = 100% ≥ 70%.
working.bn: count{O,K}=3, count{O,K,E}=3। support{O,K,E}=3/5=60% ≥ minsup। confidence = support{O,K,E}/support{O,K} = 3/3 = 100% ≥ 70%।

example.answer: Yes — support 60%, confidence 100%, so {O,K}→E is a strong rule

traps.en: Sparse index is NOT allowed on an unordered (heap) file — a sparse index needs the data sorted so one entry can stand for a whole block. Only ordered files get sparse indexes.
traps.bn: Unordered (heap) file-এ sparse index চলে না — sparse index-এর জন্য data sorted থাকতে হয় যাতে একটি entry পুরো block বোঝায়। শুধু ordered file-এ sparse index হয়।

traps.en: A secondary index cannot be sparse: since the data is not ordered on that field, every record needs its own entry, so a secondary index is always dense.
traps.bn: Secondary index sparse হতে পারে না: ঐ field-এ data ordered নয়, তাই প্রতিটি record-এর আলাদা entry লাগে, অর্থাৎ secondary index সবসময় dense।

traps.en: B-tree vs B+ tree mix-up: in a B+ tree data pointers are ONLY in the leaves and internal keys may repeat in leaves; in a B-tree every node can point to data. Range scans need the B+ tree leaf chain.
traps.bn: B-tree বনাম B+ tree গুলিয়ে ফেলা: B+ tree-তে data pointer শুধু leaf-এ এবং internal key leaf-এ আবার আসতে পারে; B-tree-তে প্রতি node data-তে point করতে পারে। Range scan-এ B+ tree leaf chain লাগে।

traps.en: Indexing does NOT always make queries faster: on low-selectivity columns or queries returning many rows, a full scan beats the index, and every index slows down INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. (Asked: Combined Bank SO(IT) 2024 — 'always faster?')
traps.bn: Indexing সবসময় query দ্রুত করে না: low-selectivity column বা অনেক row ফেরত দেওয়া query-তে full scan index-কে হারায়, আর প্রতিটি index INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ধীর করে। (এসেছে: Combined Bank SO(IT) 2024 — 'always faster?')

traps.en: Bitmap index is for LOW-cardinality columns (few distinct values), not high-cardinality ones. A common coaching key wrongly picks 'high-cardinality'; the correct answer is low-cardinality. (Asked: 49th BCS ICT 2025)
traps.bn: Bitmap index LOW-cardinality column-এর জন্য (অল্প distinct মান), high-cardinality নয়। অনেক coaching key ভুল করে 'high-cardinality' বাছে; সঠিক উত্তর low-cardinality। (এসেছে: 49th BCS ICT 2025)

traps.en: Extendible hashing: the directory doubles ONLY when the overflowing bucket's local depth equals the global depth. If local depth < global depth, only the bucket splits — the directory stays the same size.
traps.bn: Extendible hashing: directory শুধু তখন double হয় যখন overflow bucket-এর local depth = global depth। Local depth < global depth হলে শুধু bucket split হয় — directory-র আকার একই থাকে।

traps.en: Data warehouse ≠ data mining: the warehouse is the stored, integrated, historical database (OLAP); data mining is the process of finding patterns in it. The question asks for the DIFFERENCE, not a synonym.
traps.bn: Data warehouse ≠ data mining: warehouse হলো সংরক্ষিত, integrated, historical database (OLAP); data mining হলো তার মধ্যে pattern খোঁজার প্রক্রিয়া। প্রশ্নে পার্থক্য চাওয়া হয়, সমার্থক নয়।

traps.en: Star vs snowflake: star keeps dimensions denormalized (faster, some redundancy); snowflake normalizes them into sub-tables (less redundancy, more joins). Do not swap the two.
traps.bn: Star বনাম snowflake: star dimension-কে denormalized রাখে (দ্রুত, কিছু redundancy); snowflake sub-table-এ normalize করে (কম redundancy, বেশি join)। দুটো উল্টে ফেলো না।

question.en: Describe the methods of indexing and hashing in a database, and compare dense vs sparse indexes. (17th NTRCA ICT 2023; 15th NTRCA)
question.bn: একটি database-এ indexing ও hashing-এর পদ্ধতিগুলো বর্ণনা করো এবং dense ও sparse index তুলনা করো। (17th NTRCA ICT 2023; 15th NTRCA)

en: Define indexing: an auxiliary structure mapping a search key to record locations to speed retrieval.
Ordered indexes: primary (sparse, on ordering key) and secondary (dense, on non-ordering field); multilevel/B+ tree.
Hashing: a hash function maps a key to a bucket for O(1) equality search; static vs dynamic (extendible/linear).
Table: dense (entry per record) vs sparse (entry per block) — space, applicability (ordered only), search cost.
Example: a sparse index on 3000 data blocks needs 45 index blocks vs a dense index's 442.
Advantage/limitation: indexes speed reads but cost writes/space; hashing has no range support.
bn: Indexing সংজ্ঞা: search key-কে record location-এ map করা auxiliary structure, যা retrieval দ্রুত করে।
Ordered index: primary (sparse, ordering key-তে) ও secondary (dense, non-ordering field-এ); multilevel/B+ tree।
Hashing: hash function key-কে bucket-এ map করে O(1) equality search দেয়; static বনাম dynamic (extendible/linear)।
Table: dense (প্রতি record entry) বনাম sparse (প্রতি block entry) — space, প্রযোজ্যতা (শুধু ordered), search cost।
উদাহরণ: 3000 data block-এ sparse index-এ 45টি index block, dense হলে 442টি।
সুবিধা/সীমাবদ্ধতা: index read দ্রুত করে কিন্তু write/space খরচ বাড়ায়; hashing-এ range support নেই।

5.en: Define index + hashing, one dense-vs-sparse table, one line on static vs dynamic hashing.
5.bn: Index + hashing সংজ্ঞা, একটি dense-vs-sparse table, static বনাম dynamic hashing-এর এক লাইন।

10.en: Add primary/secondary/clustered index types, the sparse-index block example, and an extendible-hashing sketch.
10.bn: সাথে primary/secondary/clustered index ধরন, sparse-index block উদাহরণ ও extendible-hashing স্কেচ যোগ করো।

20.en: Add B+ tree structure and range-scan behaviour, full extendible-hashing trace, and a comparison of when to use indexing vs hashing with a worked cost.
20.bn: সাথে B+ tree structure ও range-scan আচরণ, পূর্ণ extendible-hashing trace, এবং কখন indexing বনাম hashing — worked cost সহ তুলনা যোগ করো।

question.en: Draw a B+ tree by inserting 12,14,19,30,21,22,13,34,18,23,38,40 with n=5, then delete a node. Explain fan-out and height. (BUET M.Sc. 2017; BAERA 2021)
question.bn: n=5 নিয়ে 12,14,19,30,21,22,13,34,18,23,38,40 insert করে B+ tree আঁকো, তারপর একটি node delete করো। Fan-out ও height ব্যাখ্যা করো। (BUET M.Sc. 2017; BAERA 2021)

en: State the rules for n=5: up to 5 pointers / 4 keys per node, leaves ceil((n-1)/2)=2 keys min, internal ceil(n/2)=3 pointers min.
Insert in order, splitting a full leaf by pushing the middle key up; show each split.
Draw the final tree: all keys in leaves, leaves linked in sorted order.
Delete: remove from the leaf; if it underflows, borrow from a sibling or merge and pull a key down.
Explain fan-out = pointers per node (high fan-out → shallow tree) and height ≈ log_fanout(N).
Note the range-query advantage of the leaf chain.
bn: n=5-এর নিয়ম: প্রতি node সর্বোচ্চ 5 pointer / 4 key, leaf-এ ন্যূনতম ceil((n-1)/2)=2 key, internal-এ ন্যূনতম ceil(n/2)=3 pointer।
ক্রম অনুযায়ী insert করো, full leaf split করে middle key উপরে পাঠাও; প্রতিটি split দেখাও।
চূড়ান্ত tree আঁকো: সব key leaf-এ, leaf গুলো sorted ক্রমে linked।
Delete: leaf থেকে বাদ দাও; underflow হলে sibling থেকে borrow বা merge করে key নিচে নামাও।
Fan-out = প্রতি node-এর pointer (বেশি fan-out → ছোট tree) ও height ≈ log_fanout(N) ব্যাখ্যা করো।
Leaf chain-এর range-query সুবিধা উল্লেখ করো।

10.en: Insert all keys with splits shown and draw the final B+ tree; one deletion with rebalancing.
10.bn: সব key split সহ insert করে চূড়ান্ত B+ tree আঁকো; rebalancing সহ একটি deletion।

20.en: Add the full step-by-step split trace, a deletion that triggers borrow and one that triggers merge, and the fan-out/height analysis with numbers.
20.bn: সাথে ধাপে ধাপে পূর্ণ split trace, একটি borrow ও একটি merge ঘটানো deletion, এবং সংখ্যা সহ fan-out/height বিশ্লেষণ যোগ করো।

question.en: Explain how indexing improves query performance, and whether an index always makes an application faster. (BSCL AE 2025; Combined Bank SO(IT) 2024)
question.bn: Indexing কীভাবে query performance উন্নত করে এবং index কি সবসময় application দ্রুত করে — ব্যাখ্যা করো। (BSCL AE 2025; Combined Bank SO(IT) 2024)

en: Define index and how a B+ tree turns an O(n) scan into an O(log n) lookup + range scan.
Benefits: faster WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY, covering indexes avoid table access.
When it does NOT help: low-selectivity columns, queries returning most rows, tiny tables.
Costs: extra storage, slower INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, maintenance/fragmentation.
Conclusion: indexing is a trade-off; choose columns by selectivity and read/write ratio.
bn: Index-এর সংজ্ঞা এবং B+ tree কীভাবে O(n) scan-কে O(log n) lookup + range scan করে তা বলো।
সুবিধা: দ্রুত WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY, covering index table access এড়ায়।
কখন সাহায্য করে না: low-selectivity column, বেশির ভাগ row ফেরত দেওয়া query, খুব ছোট table।
খরচ: অতিরিক্ত storage, ধীর INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, maintenance/fragmentation।
উপসংহার: indexing একটি trade-off; selectivity ও read/write অনুপাত দেখে column বাছো।

5.en: Define index, state two benefits and one case where it does not help.
5.bn: Index-এর সংজ্ঞা, দুটি সুবিধা ও একটি ক্ষেত্রে যেখানে সাহায্য করে না।

10.en: Add the B+ tree O(log n) argument, four index costs, and a Bangladeshi example (e.g. an NID lookup on a citizen table).
10.bn: সাথে B+ tree O(log n) যুক্তি, চারটি index খরচ, এবং একটি বাংলাদেশি উদাহরণ (যেমন নাগরিক table-এ NID lookup) যোগ করো।

question.en: Explain the difference between database, data warehouse and data mining with real-world examples. (Combined Bank SO(IT) 2023; 16th NTRCA ICT)
question.bn: বাস্তব উদাহরণসহ database, data warehouse ও data mining-এর পার্থক্য ব্যাখ্যা করো। (Combined Bank SO(IT) 2023; 16th NTRCA ICT)

en: Database (OLTP): operational, current, normalized data for day-to-day transactions — e.g. a bank's core account table.
Data warehouse (OLAP): integrated, historical, denormalized data for analysis — e.g. years of transactions for reporting; star/snowflake schema fed by ETL.
Data mining: the process that finds patterns in that data — classification, clustering, association (Apriori) — e.g. market-basket analysis for cross-selling.
Comparison table: purpose, data freshness, schema, users.
Relationship: OLTP feeds the warehouse via ETL; mining runs on the warehouse.
bn: Database (OLTP): দৈনন্দিন transaction-এর জন্য operational, current, normalized data — যেমন একটি bank-এর core account table।
Data warehouse (OLAP): বিশ্লেষণের জন্য integrated, historical, denormalized data — যেমন reporting-এর জন্য বছরের পর বছরের transaction; ETL-চালিত star/snowflake schema।
Data mining: সেই data-তে pattern খোঁজার প্রক্রিয়া — classification, clustering, association (Apriori) — যেমন cross-selling-এর জন্য market-basket analysis।
তুলনা table: উদ্দেশ্য, data freshness, schema, user।
সম্পর্ক: OLTP, ETL দিয়ে warehouse-কে খাওয়ায়; mining warehouse-এর উপর চলে।

5.en: Define all three with one example each and one distinguishing line.
5.bn: তিনটিরই সংজ্ঞা, প্রতিটির একটি উদাহরণ ও একটি পার্থক্যসূচক লাইন।

10.en: Add a comparison table, the ETL/OLAP-vs-OLTP contrast, and an Apriori market-basket example.
10.bn: সাথে একটি তুলনা table, ETL/OLAP-বনাম-OLTP পার্থক্য ও একটি Apriori market-basket উদাহরণ যোগ করো।

q.en: Why are all keys kept in the leaves of a B+ tree?
q.bn: B+ tree-তে সব key leaf-এ রাখা হয় কেন?

a.en: So internal nodes hold only keys + pointers (higher fan-out, shorter tree) and the linked leaves give efficient ordered range scans.
a.bn: যাতে internal node শুধু key + pointer রাখে (বেশি fan-out, ছোট tree) এবং linked leaf efficient ordered range scan দেয়।

q.en: Difference between a clustered and a non-clustered index?

a.en: A clustered index stores the rows in the index's key order (one per table); a non-clustered index is a separate structure pointing to the rows (many allowed).
a.bn: Clustered index row গুলো index key-এর ক্রমে রাখে (table-প্রতি একটি); non-clustered index আলাদা structure যা row-এ point করে (অনেক থাকতে পারে)।

q.en: When does the directory double in extendible hashing?
q.bn: Extendible hashing-এ directory কখন double হয়?

a.en: Only when a bucket overflows and its local depth equals the global depth; otherwise just the bucket splits.
a.bn: শুধু যখন একটি bucket overflow করে এবং তার local depth = global depth; নাহলে শুধু bucket split হয়।

q.en: Is a sparse index possible on a heap file?

a.en: No. A sparse index needs the file ordered on the key so one entry can represent a whole block; a heap file is unordered, so only a dense index works.
a.bn: না। Sparse index-এর জন্য file key-তে ordered হতে হয় যাতে এক entry পুরো block বোঝায়; heap file unordered, তাই শুধু dense index চলে।

q.en: What is the main difference between OLTP and OLAP?
q.bn: OLTP ও OLAP-এর মূল পার্থক্য কী?

a.en: OLTP handles many short read/write transactions on current normalized data; OLAP runs few large read-only analytical queries on historical denormalized data.
a.bn: OLTP current normalized data-তে অনেক ছোট read/write transaction চালায়; OLAP historical denormalized data-তে অল্প বড় read-only analytical query চালায়।

q.en: What does the Apriori downward-closure property say?

a.en: Every non-empty subset of a frequent itemset must also be frequent — so if {A,B} is infrequent, no superset can be frequent, which prunes candidates.
a.bn: একটি frequent itemset-এর প্রতিটি non-empty subset-ও frequent — তাই {A,B} infrequent হলে কোনো superset frequent হতে পারে না, এতে candidate prune হয়।

q.en: Why might the optimizer ignore an index you created?
q.bn: তুমি তৈরি করা index optimizer উপেক্ষা করতে পারে কেন?

a.en: If the query returns a large fraction of rows or the column has low selectivity, a full table scan reads fewer blocks than index + random row fetches.
a.bn: query যদি বেশি অংশ row ফেরত দেয় বা column-এর selectivity কম হয়, full table scan index + random row fetch-এর চেয়ে কম block পড়ে।

a.en: Star has one fact table with denormalized dimensions (fast, some redundancy); snowflake normalizes dimensions into sub-tables (less redundancy, more joins).
a.bn: Star-এ একটি fact table ও denormalized dimension (দ্রুত, কিছু redundancy); snowflake dimension-কে sub-table-এ normalize করে (কম redundancy, বেশি join)।

overview.en: Indexing and hashing are the two access paths a DBMS uses to reach a row without scanning the whole file. Ordered indexes (primary sparse, secondary dense, multilevel, B+ tree) support both equality and range access; hashing gives O(1) equality access but no ranges.
overview.bn: Indexing ও hashing হলো দুটি access path যা দিয়ে DBMS পুরো file scan না করে একটি row-তে পৌঁছায়। Ordered index (primary sparse, secondary dense, multilevel, B+ tree) equality ও range দুটোই দেয়; hashing O(1) equality দেয় কিন্তু range দেয় না।

points.en: Primary index: sparse, on the ordering key; secondary index: dense, on a non-ordering field.
points.bn: Primary index: sparse, ordering key-তে; secondary index: dense, non-ordering field-এ।

points.en: Multilevel index treats the index as a file and indexes it again until the top fits one block — reducing block reads from binary-search to the tree height.
points.bn: Multilevel index, index-কে file ধরে আবার index করে যতক্ষণ না top এক block-এ আঁটে — block read binary-search থেকে tree height-এ নামায়।

points.en: B+ tree is the dynamic multilevel index used in practice: balanced, all data pointers in leaves, leaves chained for ranges.
points.bn: B+ tree হলো বাস্তবে ব্যবহৃত dynamic multilevel index: balanced, সব data pointer leaf-এ, range-এর জন্য leaf chained।

points.en: Static hashing fixes the bucket count and suffers overflow; extendible hashing uses a directory of 2^global-depth and splits buckets on demand.
points.bn: Static hashing bucket সংখ্যা স্থির রাখে ও overflow হয়; extendible hashing 2^global-depth-এর directory ব্যবহার করে ও প্রয়োজনে bucket split করে।

question.en: A file of 3000 blocks has a sparse primary index with fan-out 68. How many block reads to find one record with a 2-level multilevel index vs binary search on a single-level index?
question.bn: 3000 block-এর একটি file-এ fan-out 68-এর sparse primary index। একটি record খুঁজতে 2-level multilevel index-এ বনাম single-level index-এ binary search-এ কতটি block read?

working.en: Single level = ceil(3000/68)=45 index blocks → binary search ceil(log2 45)+1 = 7, + 1 data read. Multilevel: L1=45, L2=ceil(45/68)=1 → 2 index reads + 1 data = 3.
working.bn: Single level = ceil(3000/68)=45 index block → binary search ceil(log2 45)+1 = 7, + 1 data read। Multilevel: L1=45, L2=ceil(45/68)=1 → 2 index read + 1 data = 3।

answer.en: Multilevel = 3 block reads vs 8 for binary search on a single level.
answer.bn: Multilevel = 3 block read, single-level binary search-এ 8।

overview.en: A data warehouse is an integrated, historical, read-mostly copy of operational data organised for analysis (OLAP), fed by ETL and modelled as star/snowflake schemas. Data mining is the step that extracts patterns from it: classification, clustering and association rules.
overview.bn: Data warehouse হলো operational data-র একটি integrated, historical, read-mostly কপি যা বিশ্লেষণের (OLAP) জন্য সাজানো, ETL দিয়ে খাওয়ানো, star/snowflake schema-তে মডেল করা। Data mining হলো সেই ধাপ যা তা থেকে pattern বের করে: classification, clustering ও association rule।

points.en: OLTP vs OLAP: transactional/current/normalized vs analytical/historical/denormalized.
points.bn: OLTP বনাম OLAP: transactional/current/normalized বনাম analytical/historical/denormalized।

points.en: Star schema = one fact table + denormalized dimensions; snowflake = normalized dimensions.
points.bn: Star schema = একটি fact table + denormalized dimension; snowflake = normalized dimension।

points.en: ETL (Extract-Transform-Load) cleans and integrates source data into the warehouse.
points.bn: ETL (Extract-Transform-Load) source data পরিষ্কার ও integrate করে warehouse-এ আনে।

points.en: Mining tasks: classification (supervised labels), clustering (unsupervised groups), association (Apriori frequent itemsets).
points.bn: Mining task: classification (supervised label), clustering (unsupervised group), association (Apriori frequent itemset)।

question.en: In 5 baskets, {milk,bread} appears in 3 and {milk} in 4. Compute support{milk,bread} and confidence milk→bread.
question.bn: 5টি basket-এ {milk,bread} 3-টিতে ও {milk} 4-টিতে আছে। support{milk,bread} ও confidence milk→bread বের করো।
